It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world where “earthly kingdoms go the way of all flesh” through violence and war, and I must ask you with a gentle spirit: why do you ask after the relationship between the “horrible pit” of suffering and the advance of the Master’s kingdom in this hour? [13, 29, 332, 1440, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who “do not spare the flock,” or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “history is His story”—a single, cohesive account of God’s glory that no “persecutor on the outside” can ever truly derail? [13, 20, 1143, 1376, 1403, 1407, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “diplomatic relations” with a culture that “mocks, vilifies, and censures” the cross, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by teaching us that the church was “born out of complete destruction” [11, 28, 138, 280, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the persecution of His saints is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “harnesses the deeds of the wicked to accomplish His good and perfect ends” [15, 68, 1143, 1446, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Blood of the Righteous from the Beginning**

**Verse**
“And He said, ‘What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground’ ” (Genesis 4:10). [1269, 1309, Conversation History]. “ ‘That on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar’ ” (Matthew 23:35). [1267, 1285, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that the “record of history” begins with a “wicked deed” where Cain was “hostile toward God, whom he could not kill, and jealous of his brother, whom he could kill” [1248, 1284, 1285, Conversation History]. Abel’s death was the first instance where the “seed of Satan” struggled against the “woman’s seed,” proving that “unbelief is the seed” of human cruelty (Genesis 3:15) [1278, 1388, Conversation History]. Yet even this first “massacre” was not hidden from the “God-Who-Sees,” for the Lord “demands a reckoning” for every “lifeblood” shed (Genesis 16:13; 9:5) [247, 589, 938, 1270, 1294, Conversation History]. The “cry of affliction” from the ground reminds us that God is the “Judge of all the earth” who will “surely hear their cry” and “administer justice for the fatherless” (Genesis 18:25; Exodus 22:23; Deuteronomy 10:18) [1299, 1316, 1321, 1328, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be terrified” by the “noise and tumult” of those who “kill the body,” for “your life is not your own” and God “will not at all acquit the wicked” (Matthew 10:28; 1 Corinthians 6:19; Exodus 23:7) [11, 227, 819, 1138, 1502, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must instead “tremble at My word” which promises that “the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptations and to reserve the unjust under punishment for the day of judgment” (Proverbs 28:26; 2 Peter 2:9) [11, 709, 858, 1313, 1406, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, “national greatness” and “military skill” were often “temporal signs” of favor, yet the Jews were warned that if they “act corruptly,” they would “soon utterly perish from the land” (Deuteronomy 28:1; 4:25–26) [409, 617, 1313, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” showing that “the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh,” for we follow a “Servant Savior” who “stooped all the way down” to a “painful, horrible, shameful death” (2 Corinthians 10:4; Philippians 2:7; Matthew 27:35) [13, 21, 32, 43, 92, 102, 551, 1081, 1313, 1426, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: Suffering as the Fuel for Gospel Advance**

**Verse**
“But I want you to know, brethren, that the things which happened to me have actually turned out for the furtherance of the gospel” (Philippians 1:12). [749, Conversation History]. “ ‘As for you, you meant evil against me; but God meant it for good, in order to bring it about as it is this day, to save many people alive’ ” (Genesis 50:20). [594, 615, 663, 692, 1312, 1361, 1501, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that God “takes the things that happen in history and in our lives and puts them together for good,” even using “stripes,” “imprisonments,” and “tumults” to “testify to the gospel of the grace of God” (Romans 8:28; Acts 20:24) [23, 146, 323, 730, 963, 1143, Conversation History]. When Saul “made havoc of the church,” the Result was that “those who were scattered went everywhere preaching the word,” proving that “the word of God is not chained” (Acts 8:3–4; 2 Timothy 2:9) [748, 750, 1132, 1268, 1283, 1420, 1504, 1646, 1720, Conversation History]. Suffering is a “lavish endowment” by which the Master “perfects, confirms, strengthens and establishes” His people, for “the testing of your faith produces patience” (1 Peter 5:10; James 1:3) [13, 31, 125, 485, 733, 747, 886, 1012, 1313, 1408, 1515, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for the Lord “raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration” (Daniel 5:26) [15, 16, 94, 201, 503, 1143, 1307, 1408, 1484, 1515, 1532, 1572, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your mind” to “dwell on whatever things are true,” refusing to let the “noise and tumult” of “troublesome times” frighten you, for “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan” (Philippians 4:8; Isaiah 46:10) [11, 20, 32, 116, 702, 1132, 1143, 1306, 1406, 1441, 1447, 1515, 1684, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Stewardship**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “animal sacrifices” were “shadows” that pointed to the Savior but could not “eliminate sin” (Hebrews 10:4) [11, 13, 32, 394, 603, 1313, 1340, 1344, 1430, 1442, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our vision of the “temple,” revealing that “your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit,” and as “living stones,” we “offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ” rather than participating in “carnal warfare” (1 Corinthians 6:19; 1 Peter 2:5) [11, 12, 13, 17, 21, 32, 67, 92, 101, 186, 238, 240, 264, 402, 440, 654, 790, 833, 937, 965, 980, 990, 1039, 1054, 1059, 1093, 1114, 1202, 1208, 1219, 1220, 1243, 1262, 1267, 1313, 1315, 1402, 1403, 1406, 1415, 1417, 1426, 1491, 1503, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Final Cry and the Victory of the Slain Lamb**

**Verse**
“And they cried with a loud voice, saying, ‘How long, O Lord, holy and true, until You judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?’ ” (Revelation 6:10). [22, 171, 187, 333, 1309, Conversation History]. “And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death” (Revelation 12:11). [1003, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “horror” of mass death by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 21, 24, 31, 103, 136, 1199, 1315, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. The martyrs under the altar represent the “church triumphant” who have been “carried by the angels to Abraham’s bosom,” having found “repose of the soul” in the “finished work” of Christ (Luke 16:22; John 19:30) [24, 31, 142, 198, 265, 1313, 1426, 1445, Conversation History]. Their “victory” is not found in “political maneuvering” but in the fact that they were “faithful until death,” for “death is but a harmless shadow for the sheep of the Good Shepherd” (Revelation 2:10; Psalm 23:4) [11, 24, 31, 142, 198, 480, 710, 789, 836, 844, 883, 916, 968, 1016, 1032, 1033, 1143, 1313, 1426, 1440, 1445, 1447, 1515, 1646, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “perfect justice will come” and He will “wipe away every tear from their eyes” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; Revelation 21:4) [13, 14, 21, 24, 32, 92, 94, 109, 121, 201, 352, 470, 712, 816, 822, 940, 948, 1132, 1143, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. You should find “tranquility of soul” by resting on the “surest foundation,” for “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan,” and the “everlasting dominion” of the King is “secure” (Daniel 7:14; 2 Timothy 2:19) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 211, 352, 412, 602, 630, 680, 803, 869, 957, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1572, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “animal sacrifices” and physical sanctuaries were “shadows” that pointed to the Savior [11, 13, 32, 142, 394, 603, 1313, 1344, 1430, 1440, 1442, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our posture, revealing that “the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands,” and we find “repose of the soul” not in “ritualized ceremonies” but in “the renewing of your mind” (Acts 7:48; Romans 12:2) [5, 11, 13, 17, 24, 101, 142, 157, 186, 238, 240, 264, 402, 464, 612, 630, 790, 833, 860, 876, 1042, 1059, 1123, 1128, 1129, 1138, 1202, 1243, 1253, 1262, 1267, 1313, 1316, 1406, 1417, 1426, 1445, 1529, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Global Church’s Mandate to Persecuted Nations**

**Verse**
“ ‘But Peter and the other apostles answered and said: “We ought to obey God rather than men” ’ ” (Acts 5:29). [48, 882, 914, 1130, 1176, 1200, 1205, 1247, 1249, 1256, 1300, 1431, 1529, 1720, Conversation History]. “ ‘Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, For theirs is the kingdom of heaven’ ” (Matthew 5:10). [983, 1198, 1229, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **Voddie Baucham** and **Paul Washer**—teaches that the church is to be a “holy place where sin is despised,” and we have an urgent mandate to “rescue those who are being led away to death” by “savage wolves” (Proverbs 24:11) [1406, 1421, 1425, Conversation History]. While we are to “be subject to the governing authorities” in mundane matters, we must “refuse to yield submission” to any state that tries to “tamper with or attempt to tone down the gospel” (Romans 13:1; Galatians 2:5) [15, 75, 1143, 1144, 1184, 1202, 1246, 1284, 1316, 1342, 1422, 1473, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. Our “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God,” recognizing that “victory that has overcome the world” is “our faith” in the “finished work” of Christ, not in “political maneuvering” (Titus 2:10; 1 John 5:4) [11, 12, 101, 361, 807, 822, 907, 934, 996, 1004, 1005, 1131, 1138, 1194, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1503, 1515, 1670, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “be bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much conflict,” and you must “pray for those who spitefully use you and persecute you” (1 Thessalonians 2:2; Matthew 5:44) [51, 76, 91, 213, 676, 1031, 1033, 1049, 1406, 1431, 1461, 1503, 1670, Conversation History]. “Trade in your worry for trust,” knowing that the “Lord Savior” will “judge between the nations,” exposing the “spirit of fraud” in every “tyrannical” regime (Isaiah 2:4; 1 Thessalonians 1:10) [11, 14, 24, 37, 94, 109, 174, 201, 210, 412, 452, 470, 719, 816, 822, 852, 948, 1143, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 335, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: Paul Tournier, a Christian physician, wrote in his A Doctor’s Casebook in the Light of the Bible: There was one patient of mine, the youngest daughter in a large family which the father found it difficult to support. One day she heard her father mutter despairingly, referring to her, “We could well have done without that one.” That is precisely what God can never say. He is a loving Father to every one of His children.3 It Defeats Selfishness Jesus included all of God’s children in His pattern for prayer. This is

system that is the enemy of God, we are not to see those in it as our personal enemies. They are captives of the real enemy, the devil (cf. 2 Tim. 2:24–26). They are not our enemies; they are our mission field. The Presence of Holiness To promote a “tranquil and quiet life,” believers must pursue “godliness and dignity.” Godliness translates “eusebeia,” a common word in the Pastoral Epistles. It carries the idea of reverence toward God. Believers should live for the majesty, holiness, love, and glory of God.
